# terminal_graphics

> A zero-dependency Rust library for drawing shapes, text and animations in a terminal's character grid with ANSI colours. Add it with `cargo add terminal_graphics`.

It draws into an in-memory grid of cells (one character plus a foreground and a background colour), then prints the grid in place. Anything drawn outside the grid is clipped, and the library never panics on out-of-range input. It has no dependencies and no unsafe code (MSRV 1.70).

## Use it when

- You want coloured text, boxes, simple shapes or animation in a terminal with very little code and no extra crates.
- You are writing a small game, demo, dashboard or visualisation that redraws the screen every frame.
- You need output you can test: `Display::render()` returns the ANSI string without touching stdout.

## Do not use it when

- You need images in the terminal (Kitty, Sixel, iTerm2 protocols). This crate is cell based, not pixel based.
- You need keyboard or mouse input. Use the companion crate `terminal_graphics_interactive` (see below), which builds on this one.
- You need widgets, layout or text boxes. Use a TUI framework for that.
- You need 24-bit colour. It has the 16 ANSI colours, and `Colour::from_rgb` picks the nearest one.

## Core types

- `Display`: the grid. `Display::new(width, height)`, `set_pixel(x, y, char, fg, bg)`, `print()`, `render()`, `write_to(writer)`, `reserve_space()`.
- `Pixel`: one cell. `Colour`: the 16 ANSI colours (`Colour::Red`, `Colour::BrightBlue`, ...).
- `Graphic`: trait for anything drawable (`draw(&self, &mut Display)`, optional `update` and `contains`).
- `Graphics`: named collection of graphics. `add`, `get_mut`, `move_by`, `remove`, `update`, `draw`, `show`.
- `Text`, `Container` (a bordered box holding one graphic), `shapes::Rect`, `shapes::Ball` (moves by its speed on `update`).
- `terminal_graphics::prelude::*` imports all of them.

Coordinates are `(x, y)` with `(0, 0)` at the top left, `x` to the right and `y` down.

## Example: an animated ball

```rust
use std::{thread::sleep, time::Duration};
use terminal_graphics::prelude::*;

fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut display = Display::new(40, 8);
    let mut graphics = Graphics::new();
    graphics
        .add("sky", Rect::new(0, 0, 40, 8, Colour::Blue))
        .add("ball", Ball::new(0.0, 3.0, 1.0, 0.0, Colour::BrightYellow))
        .add("label", Text::new(1, 0, "A ball, moving right", Colour::White, Colour::Blue));

    display.reserve_space()?; // once, before the first frame
    for _ in 0..38 {
        graphics.update(); // moves every Ball by its speed
        graphics.show(&mut display)?; // clear, draw everything, print in place
        sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Call `display.reserve_space()` once before the first frame; each frame moves the cursor up over the previous one.

## Keyboard and mouse input

This crate only draws. For key presses, mouse clicks, drags and scrolling, use the companion crate `terminal_graphics_interactive`: it re-exports everything here, so one dependency and `use terminal_graphics_interactive::prelude::*;` is enough. It is early (0.1). Add it with `cargo add terminal_graphics_interactive`.

It works in Windows PowerShell, Windows Terminal, Linux and macOS terminals, and over SSH. See https://github.com/calum/terminal_graphics_interactive for its own `llms.txt`.
